groups.title: Relationships Within the Trinity
groups.note: The terms eternal generation, procession, perichoresis, and inseparable operations are theological formulations that explain the combined biblical witness.

essence.def: Essence means what God is. It is also called God’s being or substance. There is only one divine essence, and the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit each have it fully, so They are one God, not three.

nature.def: A nature is the kind of thing something is, along with everything that belongs to being that kind of thing. The divine nature includes being eternal, all-powerful and all-knowing, and human nature includes having a body and a soul. When we speak of God, “nature” means much the same as “essence”: what God is.

person.def: In speaking of God, a Person is who someone is, as distinct from what they are: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three Persons, yet one God. The word does not mean three separate beings, three parts of God, or three individuals the way three humans are; each Person is the whole one God. The Persons differ from one another only in how They are related: the Father begets, the Son is begotten, and the Spirit proceeds.

trinity.def: The Trinity is the name Christians use for the one God who exists as three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. The word itself is not found in the Bible. But it sums up what the Bible teaches: there is only one God, and the Father, the Son and the Spirit are each fully God.

eternal.def: Eternal means without beginning and without end. God has always existed and always will. He is not bound by time as we are, because He made time itself.

immutable.def: Immutable means unchanging. God does not change in His nature or His character. He does not grow, fade, or become better or worse, so He can always be trusted to be who He is.

omnipresent.def: Omnipresent means present everywhere. God is not limited by space. Yet He is not spread out with a small piece of Him in each place; He is wholly present everywhere at once.

indivisible.def: Indivisible means that God has no parts and cannot be divided. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not three pieces of God, and qualities such as His love and His justice are not separate parts of Him either. This teaching is sometimes called divine simplicity.

coeternal.def: Coeternal means equally eternal. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit have all existed forever. None of the Persons existed before another, and there was never a time when the Son or the Spirit did not exist.

coequal.def: Coequal means fully equal. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are equal in deity, power and glory. None is a lesser or junior God, and each is to be worshipped and honoured alike.

perichoresis.def: Perichoresis is a Greek word for the way the three Persons of the Trinity dwell in one another. Each Person is fully in the others and shares one life with Them. Yet They do not merge or lose what makes each Person distinct.

eternal-generation.def: Eternal generation describes the Son being “begotten” of the Father, the word used for how the Son comes from the Father. It has no beginning in time and involves nothing bodily: the Father did not produce the Son the way human parents have children. The Father eternally gives the whole divine essence to the Son, so this does not divide God or make a second God; the Son is fully God, one with the Father.

procession.def: Procession is the Holy Spirit’s eternal coming forth from the Father and the Son, as from one source. It is different from begetting: the Son is begotten of the Father, while the Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son together, and these are two distinct ways of coming forth. It is also not the same as the Spirit being sent at Pentecost, which happened at a point in time; procession has no beginning and belongs to who the Spirit eternally is.

relations-of-origin.def: Relations of origin are what tell the three divine Persons apart. The Father begets the Son and is unbegotten, which means He comes from no one; the Son is begotten of the Father; and the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son. The Persons are not set apart by different natures or ranks, since each is fully and equally the one God, but only by these relations to one another.

inseparable-operations.def: Inseparable operations means that every work God does outside Himself, such as creating, saving or giving life, is done by all three Persons together as one act. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit never work apart or split a task between Them. Yet each Person acts in His own way within that one work.

appropriation.def: Appropriation means speaking of a work that all three Persons share as belonging especially to one Person. For example, creation is often linked to the Father, redemption to the Son, and making us holy (sanctification) to the Spirit. This does not deny that the other Persons act too; it simply helps us see how each Person is fitting for that work.

incarnation.def: The Incarnation is the Son of God becoming man. Without ceasing to be God, He took a full human nature, with a real human body and a human soul. He was born as Jesus of Nazareth.

hypostatic-union.def: The hypostatic union is the joining of the divine nature and a human nature in the one Person of the Son. “Hypostatic” comes from a Greek word meaning person. The two natures are not mixed or changed into each other, and they are never divided or separated, so Jesus is one Person, truly God and truly man.

essence.def: சாராம்சம் என்பது தேவன் என்னவாக இருக்கிறார் என்பதைக் குறிக்கிறது. இது தேவனுடைய உள்ளமை அல்லது உட்பொருள் என்றும் அழைக்கப்படுகிறது. தெய்வீக சாராம்சம் ஒன்றே ஒன்றுதான். பிதா, குமாரன், பரிசுத்த ஆவியானவர் ஒவ்வொருவரும் அதை முழுமையாகக் கொண்டிருக்கிறார்கள். ஆகவே அவர்கள் மூன்று தேவர்கள் அல்ல, ஒரே தேவன்.

nature.def: ஒன்று எந்த வகையைச் சேர்ந்தது என்பதே அதன் சுபாவம். அந்த வகையாக இருப்பதற்கு உரிய எல்லாமும் அதில் அடங்கும். தெய்வீக சுபாவத்தில் நித்தியமாக இருப்பது, சர்வவல்லமை உள்ளவராக இருப்பது, எல்லாவற்றையும் அறிந்தவராக இருப்பது ஆகியவை அடங்கும். மனித சுபாவத்தில் சரீரமும் ஆத்துமாவும் உடையவராக இருப்பது அடங்கும். தேவனைப் பற்றிப் பேசும்போது, ‘சுபாவம்’ என்பது ஏறக்குறைய ‘சாராம்சம்’ என்பதன் பொருளையே தருகிறது: அதாவது, தேவன் என்னவாக இருக்கிறார் என்பதே.

person.def: தேவனைப் பற்றிப் பேசும்போது, ஆள்தத்துவம் என்பது ஒருவர் ‘என்னவாக’ இருக்கிறார் என்பதை அல்ல, அவர் ‘யார்’ என்பதைக் குறிக்கிறது. பிதா, குமாரன், பரிசுத்த ஆவியானவர் மூன்று ஆள்தத்துவங்கள்; ஆனாலும் அவர்கள் ஒரே தேவன். இந்த வார்த்தை தனித்தனியான மூன்று உள்ளமைகளையோ, தேவனுடைய மூன்று பகுதிகளையோ, மூன்று மனிதர்கள் இருப்பதுபோல மூன்று தனிநபர்களையோ குறிப்பதில்லை. ஒவ்வொரு ஆள்தத்துவமும் முழுமையான அந்த ஒரே தேவனாக இருக்கிறார். ஆள்தத்துவங்கள் ஒருவரோடொருவர் கொண்டுள்ள உறவின் முறையில் மட்டுமே வேறுபடுகிறார்கள்: பிதா ஜெனிப்பிக்கிறார், குமாரன் ஜெனிப்பிக்கப்படுகிறார், ஆவியானவர் புறப்படுகிறார்.

trinity.def: திரித்துவம் என்பது, பிதா, குமாரன், பரிசுத்த ஆவியானவர் என்னும் மூன்று ஆள்தத்துவங்களாக இருக்கிற ஒரே தேவனைக் குறிக்கக் கிறிஸ்தவர்கள் பயன்படுத்தும் பெயர். ‘திரித்துவம்’ என்ற வார்த்தை வேதாகமத்தில் காணப்படுவதில்லை. ஆனால் வேதாகமம் போதிப்பதை அது சுருக்கமாகச் சொல்கிறது: தேவன் ஒருவரே; பிதா, குமாரன், ஆவியானவர் ஒவ்வொருவரும் முழுமையாக தேவனாக இருக்கிறார்கள்.

eternal.def: நித்தியம் என்பது ஆரம்பமும் முடிவும் இல்லாத நிலையைக் குறிக்கிறது. தேவன் எப்போதும் இருந்து வருகிறார், என்றென்றும் இருப்பார். நம்மைப் போல அவர் காலத்திற்குக் கட்டுப்பட்டவர் அல்ல. ஏனென்றால் காலத்தையே உண்டாக்கியவர் அவர்தான்.

immutable.def: மாறாத்தன்மை என்றால் மாறாமல் இருப்பது என்று பொருள். தேவன் தமது சுபாவத்திலும் தமது குணத்திலும் மாறுவதில்லை. அவர் வளருவதில்லை, மங்கிப்போவதுமில்லை. அவர் முன்பைவிட மேலானவராகவோ தாழ்ந்தவராகவோ ஆவதுமில்லை. ஆகவே, அவர் எப்போதும் தாம் இருக்கிறபடியே இருப்பார் என்று நாம் அவரை நம்பலாம்.

omnipresent.def: சர்வவியாபி என்றால் எல்லா இடங்களிலும் இருக்கிறவர் என்று பொருள். தேவன் இடத்தால் கட்டுப்படுத்தப்படுவதில்லை. ஆனாலும், ஒவ்வொரு இடத்திலும் தம்முடைய ஒரு சிறு பகுதி இருக்கும்படி அவர் பரவியிருப்பதில்லை. அவர் ஒரே நேரத்தில் எல்லா இடங்களிலும் முழுமையாக இருக்கிறார்.

indivisible.def: பிரிக்கமுடியாத்தன்மை என்றால், தேவனுக்குப் பகுதிகள் இல்லை, அவரைப் பிரிக்கவும் முடியாது என்று பொருள். பிதா, குமாரன், பரிசுத்த ஆவியானவர் ஆகியோர் தேவனுடைய மூன்று துண்டுகள் அல்ல. அவருடைய அன்பு, அவருடைய நீதி போன்ற பண்புகளும் அவருடைய தனித்தனிப் பகுதிகள் அல்ல. இந்தப் போதனை சில நேரங்களில் தேவனுடைய எளிமை என்று அழைக்கப்படுகிறது.

coeternal.def: சம நித்தியம் என்றால் சம அளவில் நித்தியமாக இருப்பது என்று பொருள். பிதாவும், குமாரனும், பரிசுத்த ஆவியானவரும் என்றென்றும் இருந்து வருகிறார்கள். ஆள்தத்துவங்களில் எவரும் மற்றொருவருக்கு முன்பு இருந்ததில்லை. குமாரனோ ஆவியானவரோ இல்லாதிருந்த ஒரு காலம் ஒருபோதும் இருந்ததில்லை.

coequal.def: சமத்துவம் என்றால் முழுமையாகச் சமமாக இருப்பது என்று பொருள். பிதா, குமாரன், பரிசுத்த ஆவியானவர் ஆகியோர் தேவத்துவத்திலும், வல்லமையிலும், மகிமையிலும் சமமானவர்கள். அவர்களில் எவரும் குறைந்த தேவனோ கீழ்நிலைத் தேவனோ அல்ல. ஒவ்வொருவரும் ஒரே விதமாக ஆராதிக்கப்படவும் கனப்படுத்தப்படவும் வேண்டியவர்.

perichoresis.def: பரஸ்பர உள்ளுறைதல் (பெரிகொரேசிஸ்) என்பது ஒரு கிரேக்கச் சொல். திரித்துவத்தின் மூன்று ஆள்தத்துவங்களும் ஒருவருக்குள் ஒருவர் வாசமாயிருக்கும் விதத்தை இது குறிக்கிறது. ஒவ்வொரு ஆள்தத்துவமும் மற்ற ஆள்தத்துவங்களில் முழுமையாக இருக்கிறார். அவர்களோடு ஒரே ஜீவனைப் பகிர்ந்துகொள்கிறார். ஆனாலும் அவர்கள் ஒருவரோடொருவர் கலந்து ஒன்றாகிவிடுவதில்லை. ஒவ்வொரு ஆள்தத்துவத்தையும் தனித்துவமாக்குவதை அவர்கள் இழப்பதுமில்லை.

eternal-generation.def: நித்திய ஜெனிப்பித்தல் என்பது குமாரன் பிதாவினால் “ஜெனிப்பிக்கப்பட்டவர்” என்பதைக் குறிக்கிறது. குமாரன் பிதாவிடமிருந்து எப்படி வருகிறார் என்பதைச் சொல்ல இந்தச் சொல் பயன்படுகிறது. இதற்குக் காலத்தில் தொடக்கம் இல்லை. இதில் சரீரப்பிரகாரமான எதுவும் இல்லை. மனிதப் பெற்றோர் பிள்ளைகளைப் பெறுவதுபோல பிதா குமாரனை உண்டாக்கவில்லை. பிதா தெய்வீக சாராம்சம் முழுவதையும் நித்தியமாகக் குமாரனுக்குக் கொடுக்கிறார். ஆகவே இது தேவனைப் பிரிப்பதில்லை. இரண்டாவது ஒரு தேவனை உண்டாக்குவதுமில்லை. குமாரன் முழுமையாகத் தேவனாக இருக்கிறார்; பிதாவோடு ஒன்றாக இருக்கிறார்.

procession.def: புறப்படுதல் என்பது பரிசுத்த ஆவியானவர் பிதாவிடமிருந்தும் குமாரனிடமிருந்தும், ஒரே மூலத்திலிருந்து என்பதுபோல, நித்தியமாக வெளிவருவதைக் குறிக்கிறது. இது ஜெனிப்பித்தலிலிருந்து வேறுபட்டது. குமாரன் பிதாவினால் ஜெனிப்பிக்கப்பட்டவர். ஆவியானவரோ பிதாவிடமிருந்தும் குமாரனிடமிருந்தும் ஒன்றாகப் புறப்படுகிறார். இவை இரண்டும் வெளிவருதலின் வெவ்வேறான இரண்டு விதங்கள். மேலும், பெந்தெகொஸ்தே நாளில் ஆவியானவர் அனுப்பப்பட்டதும் புறப்படுதலும் ஒன்றல்ல. அனுப்பப்பட்டது காலத்தில் ஒரு குறிப்பிட்ட நேரத்தில் நடந்தது. புறப்படுதலுக்கோ தொடக்கம் இல்லை. அது ஆவியானவர் நித்தியமாக யாராக இருக்கிறார் என்பதைச் சார்ந்தது.

relations-of-origin.def: தோற்ற உறவுகள் என்பவை மூன்று தெய்வீக ஆள்தத்துவங்களையும் ஒருவரிடமிருந்து ஒருவரை வேறுபடுத்திக் காட்டுபவை. பிதா குமாரனை ஜெனிப்பிக்கிறார். அவர் ஜெனிப்பிக்கப்படாதவர்; அதாவது, அவர் யாரிடமிருந்தும் வருவதில்லை. குமாரன் பிதாவினால் ஜெனிப்பிக்கப்பட்டவர். பரிசுத்த ஆவியானவர் பிதாவிடமிருந்தும் குமாரனிடமிருந்தும் புறப்படுகிறார். ஆள்தத்துவங்கள் வெவ்வேறு சுபாவங்களாலோ வெவ்வேறு நிலைகளாலோ வேறுபடுத்தப்படுவதில்லை. ஏனெனில் ஒவ்வொருவரும் முழுமையாகவும் சமமாகவும் அந்த ஒரே தேவனாக இருக்கிறார். ஒருவரோடொருவர் கொண்டுள்ள இந்த உறவுகளால் மட்டுமே அவர்கள் வேறுபடுத்தப்படுகிறார்கள்.

inseparable-operations.def: தேவன் தமக்கு வெளியே பல கிரியைகளைச் செய்கிறார். உதாரணமாக, படைத்தல், இரட்சித்தல், ஜீவன் கொடுத்தல். இப்படிப்பட்ட ஒவ்வொரு கிரியையையும் மூன்று ஆள்தத்துவங்களும் சேர்ந்து ஒரே செயலாகச் செய்கிறார்கள். இதுவே பிரிக்கமுடியாத செயல்பாடுகள் என்பதன் பொருள். பிதாவும் குமாரனும் பரிசுத்த ஆவியானவரும் ஒருபோதும் தனித்தனியாகச் செயல்படுவதில்லை. ஒரு வேலையைத் தங்களுக்குள் பங்கிட்டுக்கொள்வதும் இல்லை. ஆனாலும், அந்த ஒரே கிரியைக்குள் ஒவ்வொரு ஆள்தத்துவமும் தமக்கே உரிய விதத்தில் செயல்படுகிறார்.

appropriation.def: மூன்று ஆள்தத்துவங்களும் சேர்ந்து செய்யும் ஒரு கிரியையை, குறிப்பாக ஒரே ஆள்தத்துவத்திற்கு உரியதாகப் பேசுவதே உரித்தாக்குதல் ஆகும். உதாரணமாக, படைப்பு பெரும்பாலும் பிதாவோடு இணைத்துப் பேசப்படுகிறது. மீட்பு குமாரனோடும், நம்மைப் பரிசுத்தமாக்குதல் பரிசுத்த ஆவியானவரோடும் இணைத்துப் பேசப்படுகின்றன. மற்ற ஆள்தத்துவங்களும் செயல்படுகிறார்கள் என்பதை இது மறுப்பதில்லை. அந்தக் கிரியைக்கு ஒவ்வொரு ஆள்தத்துவமும் எப்படிப் பொருத்தமானவர் என்பதைக் காண இது நமக்கு உதவுகிறது, அவ்வளவுதான்.

incarnation.def: மனுவுருவாதல் என்பது தேவனுடைய குமாரன் மனிதனானதைக் குறிக்கிறது. அவர் தேவனாக இருப்பதை விட்டுவிடாமலேயே, முழுமையான ஒரு மனித சுபாவத்தை எடுத்துக்கொண்டார். அதில் உண்மையான மனித சரீரமும் மனித ஆத்துமாவும் உண்டு. அவர் நாசரேத்தூர் இயேசுவாகப் பிறந்தார்.

hypostatic-union.def: ஆள்தத்துவ ஐக்கியம் என்பது, தெய்வீக சுபாவமும் ஒரு மனித சுபாவமும் குமாரன் என்ற ஒரே ஆள்தத்துவத்தில் இணைக்கப்பட்டிருப்பதாகும். ‘ஹைப்போஸ்டாடிக்’ (hypostatic) என்ற சொல், ‘ஆள்தத்துவம்’ என்று பொருள்படும் ஒரு கிரேக்கச் சொல்லிலிருந்து வருகிறது. இந்த இரண்டு சுபாவங்களும் ஒன்றோடொன்று கலப்பதில்லை. ஒன்று மற்றொன்றாக மாறுவதும் இல்லை. அவை ஒருபோதும் பகுக்கப்படுவதோ பிரிக்கப்படுவதோ இல்லை. ஆகவே இயேசு ஒரே ஆள்தத்துவமாக இருக்கிறார். அவர் மெய்யாகவே தேவனும், மெய்யாகவே மனிதனுமாக இருக்கிறார்.

teachings.title: God is One
teachings.detail: There is only one true God, not three Gods.
teachings.cap: Each Person is God, and all three are the one God at the centre. There are not three Gods.
teachings.meaning: There is only one divine being, and nothing else shares in being God. Christians say God is one in essence, or nature, which means what God is. He is also three in Person, which means who God is: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. These are not two ways of counting the same thing, so there is no contradiction: there is one “what” and three “who.” This rules out belief in many gods. It also rules out thinking of the Father, the Son and the Spirit as three separate gods who work together like a team.
teachings.support: Deuteronomy 6:4 is Israel’s basic confession of faith: the LORD is One, so no other god stands beside Him to share His worship. In Isaiah 45:5, God Himself says there is no God but Him, which shuts out every rival, and Paul says the same in 1 Corinthians 8:4, showing that the first Christians held this belief too. These passages state plainly that God is one, but the further teaching that He is one in essence and three in Person is drawn from them together with other passages that show the Father, the Son and the Spirit each to be God.

verses.label: Deuteronomy 6:4
verses.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.

verses.label: Isaiah 45:5
verses.text: I am the LORD, and there is no other; there is no God but Me. I will equip you for battle, though you have not known Me,

verses.label: 1 Corinthians 8:4
verses.text: So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.

topic.title: How can the Son and Spirit be God without there being more than one God?
topic.theme: One God: Monotheism and the Trinity
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that confessing the Son and Spirit as God introduces neither a second or third God nor a single Person under several names: Hilary, Hippolytus, Ambrose, Augustine, Novatian, Waterland and Bickersteth all reject the Sabellian or modalist reading, and Hilary, Ambrose, Augustine, Waterland, Bickersteth and Warfield read texts like 1 Corinthians 8:6 and 'I and the Father are one' as including the Son in the one God while keeping the Persons distinct.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: I shall take care that in our assertion of the One true God I give no cover to the Sabellian heresy that the Father is one Person with the Son

teachings.title: God is Spirit
teachings.detail: God is not inherently a material or bodily being.
teachings.cap: God is Spirit. The dotted circle holds no body and no material parts.
teachings.meaning: God is not made of matter. He has no body, no size or shape, and no physical parts, so He cannot be seen with our eyes or confined to one place. This rules out thinking of God as a larger, stronger version of a human being. When the Bible speaks of God’s hand or His eyes, it uses pictures from our world to describe His real power and care. The Son did take a real human body in the Incarnation, but He added that human nature to Himself; the divine nature itself never became physical.
teachings.support: In John 4:24 Jesus states the teaching plainly: God is Spirit. So true worship is not tied to one holy mountain or building. In Luke 24:39 the risen Jesus shows what “spirit” means when He says that “a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.” Read together, the two passages show that being Spirit means having no body. The body Jesus shows His disciples is the human body the Son took when He became man.

verses.label: John 4:24
verses.text: God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”

verses.label: Luke 24:39
verses.text: Look at My hands and My feet. It is I Myself. Touch Me and see—for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.”

topic.title: Does God have a body or passions, and how is Scripture's bodily language to be read?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: All the authors who address the question agree that God has no body and that Scripture's bodily and emotional language is not to be taken literally.

quote.author: Daniel Waterland
quote.text: We, more consistently, suppose three Persons equal, in all respects; none of them singly part of God; but every one perfect God.

teachings.title: God is Eternal
teachings.detail: God has no beginning or end.
teachings.cap: The unbroken circle: God has no beginning and no end.
teachings.meaning: There was never a time when God did not exist, and there will never be a time when He stops existing. Nothing made Him or brought Him into being. He simply is, and everything else depends on Him. He is not merely very old, and He does not grow older, because time is something He created, not something that rules over Him; so He was never new or unfinished, and He will never wear out or pass away.
teachings.support: Psalm 90:2 looks back to before the mountains and the earth existed and says God was already there: “from everlasting to everlasting You are God.” That means there is no beginning behind Him and no end ahead of Him. In Revelation 1:8 the Lord calls Himself “the Alpha and the Omega,” the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, the One “who is and was and is to come,” so He stands at the start and the finish of all things; the further point that God is not bound by time is a conclusion drawn from passages like these together with the Bible’s teaching that He made all things.

verses.label: Psalm 90:2
verses.text: Before the mountains were born or You brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting You are God.

verses.label: Revelation 1:8
verses.text: “I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, who is and was and is to come—the Almighty.

topic.title: Is God eternal and unchangeable, beyond time and increase?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that God is eternal and unchangeable: Gregory of Nyssa, Augustine, Athanasius, Novatian, Ambrose and Irenaeus each deny that the divine nature has a beginning, increase, loss, temporal succession, deliberation over the uncertain, or emptiness.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: Since, then, it belongs to the creation to have a beginning, that will be alien from the uncreated nature which belongs to the creation.

teachings.title: God is Uncreated
teachings.detail: God exists independently of creation.
teachings.cap: The arrow runs one way. Creation depends on God, and God depends on nothing He made.
teachings.meaning: God was never made, caused or brought into being by anyone or anything. He simply is, without beginning, and He does not depend on the world for anything, while everything else depends completely on Him. This rules out any idea that God came into being, grew out of the universe, or is one part of the created world, however great. It also means that the Son and the Holy Spirit are not created beings, but are fully the one uncreated God with the Father.
teachings.support: In Acts 17:24–25, God is the One who “made the world and everything in it,” and He is not served “as if He needed anything,” because He is the giver of “life and breath and everything else.” So He stands outside creation as its Maker, not as one more thing that needs to be kept alive. John 1:3 says that “without Him nothing was made that has been made,” which places the Word, the Son, on the side of the Maker rather than among the things made. The word “uncreated” does not appear in either passage. It is a conclusion drawn from these passages taken together.

verses.label: Acts 17:24–25
verses.text: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands. Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.

verses.label: John 1:3
verses.text: Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made.

topic.title: How does God's nature transcend creatures, and does He need anything from them?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that God transcends creatures and needs nothing from them, but they come at this from different angles.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: for he from whom death is not absent is not in his essence immortal. But again; if these terms signify the absence neither of death nor of destruction, either they are applied falsely to the God overall, or else they comprise within themselves some different meaning.

teachings.title: God is Immutable
teachings.detail: God’s divine nature does not change.
teachings.cap: The double circle stands for a nature that does not change.
teachings.meaning: God never becomes more or less than He is. He does not grow wiser, stronger or kinder over time, and He does not weaken, age or wear out. His goodness, faithfulness and love are the same today as they have always been, so His promises can be fully relied on. This does not mean God is cold or inactive: He truly acts in history, answers prayer and deals with people as they change, but He Himself stays the same in who He is.
teachings.support: In Malachi 3:6 the LORD says plainly, “I, the LORD, do not change,” and gives this as the reason Jacob’s descendants were not destroyed: because God stays faithful to His promises, His people are kept safe. In James 1:17 God is called the Father of the heavenly lights, “with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.” Unlike the sun and stars, which move and cast changing shadows, God is always the same. These verses speak directly about God not changing, and the full teaching that nothing in His divine nature ever changes is drawn from them together with what the Bible says about God being eternal.

verses.label: Malachi 3:6
verses.text: “Because I, the LORD, do not change, you descendants of Jacob have not been destroyed.

verses.label: James 1:17
verses.text: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.

topic.title: How do God's knowledge, will and creative action work without change or succession?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: Augustine, Gregory of Nyssa and Hilary agree that God's knowledge and will involve no change, learning or succession.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: Still Further of the Difference Between the Knowledge…
quote.text: He does not know them because they are, but they are because He knows them. For He was not ignorant of what He was about to create; therefore He created because He knew; He did not know because He created.

teachings.title: God is Invisible
teachings.detail: The divine essence cannot be seen by physical eyes.
teachings.cap: The divine essence cannot be seen with physical eyes. The Son makes the Father known.
teachings.meaning: God is not made of matter and has no body, so nothing about what He is could be seen by eyes, however sharp. This rules out picturing God as a very large or very bright creature, or thinking that any statue or image could show what He truly is. When the Bible tells of people “seeing” God, He was showing Himself through something visible, such as fire, a cloud or a vision, not letting them look on His very being. Even when the Son became man and could be seen, people saw His real human body, while His divine nature stayed beyond sight.
teachings.support: 1 Timothy 1:17 says it plainly, calling God “invisible” alongside “eternal” and “immortal.” John 1:18 adds that “No one has ever seen God,” yet the Son, “who is Himself God,” has made Him known, so we come to know the unseen God through the Son, not by sight. That God has no body at all is a conclusion drawn from these passages together with others, such as Jesus’ teaching that God is spirit.

verses.label: 1 Timothy 1:17
verses.text: Now to the King eternal, immortal, and invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.

verses.label: John 1:18
verses.text: No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known.

topic.title: How can the invisible Father be known and seen through the Son?
topic.theme: God the Father
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that the invisible Father is known only through the Son, and none thinks God can be seen by natural power or comprehended in his essence.

quote.author: Novatian
quote.place: He Proves Also that the Words Spoken to Philip Make…
quote.text: But if Christ Himself had been the Father, why did He promise as future, a reward which He had already granted and given?

teachings.title: God is Omnipresent
teachings.detail: God is not limited by physical space.
teachings.cap: The circles spread outward: God fills every place and no place contains Him.
teachings.meaning: There is no place where God is absent, from the room you are sitting in to the farthest star. God is not a huge being stretched across the universe, with a little of Him here and a little of Him there. Because He has no parts, the whole of God is present in every place at once. This does not mean that God is the same thing as the world, or that the world contains Him. He made all things and is distinct from them, yet no one and nothing is ever beyond His reach.
teachings.support: In Psalm 139:7–10 the writer imagines going up to the heavens, down to Sheol (the place of the dead), and out to the farthest sea, and each time he finds God already there: “Your right hand will hold me fast.” In Jeremiah 23:24 the LORD asks, “Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?”, so no one can hide from Him. These passages show that there is no place without God. That He is present whole and undivided in every place is a conclusion drawn from them together with the Bible’s wider teaching about God’s oneness, not something either verse states in those words.

verses.label: Psalm 139:7–10
verses.text: Where can I go to escape Your Spirit? Where can I flee from Your presence? If I ascend to the heavens, You are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, You are there. If I rise on the wings of the dawn, if I settle by the farthest sea, even there Your hand will guide me; Your right hand will hold me fast.

verses.label: Jeremiah 23:24
verses.text: “Can a man hide in secret places where I cannot see him?” declares the LORD. “Do I not fill the heavens and the earth?” declares the LORD.

topic.title: Is God present everywhere without being contained in a place?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: All the authors (Hilary of Poitiers, Novatian, Gregory of Nyssa, Irenaeus of Lyons, Athanasius and Augustine) agree that God is everywhere and confined by no place, containing all things rather than being contained, though they draw different consequences from this.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: There is no space where God is not; space does not exist apart from Him. He is in heaven, in hell, beyond the seas; dwelling in all things and enveloping all.

teachings.title: God is Indivisible
teachings.detail: God’s essence is not divided into parts.
teachings.cap: One undivided being. The Persons are not three pieces of God.
teachings.meaning: God is not built out of pieces that have been put together, and He cannot be split up. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not three parts that add up to one God, like a pie cut into three slices. Each Person is the whole God. In the same way, God’s love, justice and power are not separate parts of Him. His love is simply God Himself loving, and His justice is God Himself being just, so no part of God can be lost, taken away, or set against another part.
teachings.support: In Deuteronomy 6:4, Israel is told that “the LORD is One.” This means there is only one God, not a group of gods or a collection of pieces. In John 10:30, Jesus says, “I and the Father are one,” yet He does not mean that He and the Father are two halves of God, for elsewhere the Bible shows that each is fully God. The Bible never uses the word “indivisible.” The church drew this conclusion from passages like these taken together: God is one, and the Father, the Son and the Spirit are each fully God, so God cannot be made of parts.

verses.label: Deuteronomy 6:4
verses.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.

verses.label: John 10:30
verses.text: I and the Father are one.”

topic.title: Is God simple, so that His attributes and names are identical with His essence?
topic.theme: The Divine Nature and Attributes
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that God is simple and without parts, change or accidents, so His attributes are not things He has apart from Himself.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: for it will not be possible, if God is essentially Father, to exclude the Son from a relationship to Him thus essential.

teachings.title: God has one divine essence
teachings.detail: The three Persons possess the same undivided divine being.
teachings.cap: Solid lines: each Person is God. Dashed lines: no Person is another. One being, three Persons.
teachings.meaning: There are two different questions we can ask about God: what is He, and who is He? The answer to “what” is one: there is only one divine essence, one being that is God, and the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit each have all of it, not a share or a slice. The answer to “who” is three: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three distinct Persons, but They are not three beings or three gods standing side by side like three people in a room. So the Trinity is neither three gods joined together nor one God wearing three masks; it is one being, wholly possessed by three Persons.
teachings.support: In John 10:30 Jesus says, “I and the Father are one.” He speaks of two (“I and the Father”), so He does not claim to be the same Person as the Father, yet He says They are one, not merely in purpose but, as the rest of Scripture shows, in the very being of God. Hebrews 1:3 calls the Son “the exact representation of His nature,” meaning the Son is distinct from the Father yet has the very same divine nature, not a lesser or separate one. Neither verse uses the word “essence”; the teaching is a conclusion drawn from passages like these together with the Bible’s clear teaching that there is only one God.

verses.label: John 10:30
verses.text: I and the Father are one.”

verses.label: Hebrews 1:3
verses.text: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

topic.title: In what does the unity of the one God consist?
topic.theme: One God: Monotheism and the Trinity
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that God's unity is not that of a single solitary Person: Waterland denies that the Godhead is monoprosopos (equating that with Sabellian singularity), Hilary reads 'Believe in God, believe also in Me' as excluding a solitary God, and Athanasius rejects the Marcellian expansion-and-contraction of the Monad as leading to Sabellianism.

quote.author: Daniel Waterland
quote.text: it is from thence we discover that God is not μονοπρόσωπος, a single Hypostasis, but that the Father has his coessential and coeternal Son and Holy Spirit always in him and with him.

teachings.title: The Father is God
teachings.detail: The Father is fully God, the source of all things and the one to whom Jesus prays.
teachings.cap: The Father is God: the line joins the Father to the one God.
teachings.meaning: Calling God “Father” is more than a picture of His care for us. Within the one God, the Father is the Person who eternally begets the Son, while He Himself comes from no one. He has the whole divine essence, everything it means to be God, so He is eternal, all-powerful and all-knowing. Yet being the Father does not make Him more God than the Son or the Spirit, or older than Them, and it is not just a role God plays for a time: He is a real Person, distinct from the Son and the Spirit, and He has always been Father because the Son has always been with Him.
teachings.support: In John 6:27 Jesus speaks plainly of “God the Father,” and He shows that the Father is distinct from Himself, since it is the Father who places His seal of approval on the Son of Man. In 1 Corinthians 8:6 Paul names the Father as the “one God … from whom all things came,” the source of everything that exists. In the same verse Paul calls Jesus the “one Lord … through whom all things came,” so the Father being God does not put the Son outside the one God; that the Son and the Spirit are also fully God is shown from other passages taken together.

verses.label: John 6:27
verses.text: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.”

verses.label: 1 Corinthians 8:6
verses.text: yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.

topic.title: What is proper to the Father, and how do believers relate to him?
topic.theme: God the Father
topic.cmp: The five authors answer different questions, so they mostly complement rather than contradict one another.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: What is Said of the Father and Son Together, and What Not.
quote.text: if nothing is spoken of the Father as such, except that which is spoken of Him in relation to the Son, that is, that He is His father, or begetter, or beginning

teachings.title: The Son is God
teachings.detail: Jesus, the Son, is fully God, not a created being or a lesser god.
teachings.cap: The Son is God: the line joins the Son to the one God.
teachings.meaning: To say the Son is God means He has the very same divine nature as the Father, not merely a similar or lesser one. Everything that makes God God belongs to the Son fully: He is eternal, all-powerful, and rightly worshipped. This rules out the idea that the Son is the first and greatest thing God made, or a half-divine being, or a second god beside the Father. He is still not the Father; He is a distinct Person, yet He shares the one being of God with the Father and the Holy Spirit.
teachings.support: In John 1:1 the Word already existed “in the beginning,” was “with God,” and “was God.” So He is distinct from the Father, yet He is truly God, and John goes on to show that this Word is Jesus. In John 20:28 Thomas calls the risen Jesus “My Lord and my God!” and Jesus accepts this rather than correcting him, while in Hebrews 1:8 God Himself speaks to the Son as “O God” and gives Him an everlasting throne.

verses.label: John 1:1
verses.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

verses.label: John 20:28
verses.text: Thomas replied, “My Lord and my God!”

verses.label: Hebrews 1:8
verses.text: But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.

topic.title: Is the Son truly and fully God, equal with the Father?
topic.theme: The Full Deity of the Son
topic.cmp: All the authors who answer agree that the Son is truly God and not a creature or lesser deity: Irenaeus, Novatian, Athanasius, Hilary, Gregory of Nyssa, Basil, Ambrose, Augustine, Owen, Waterland and Bickersteth each affirm this, and Basil and Athanasius read the session at the right hand as equality, not lower rank.

quote.author: Irenaeus of Lyons
quote.place: Chapter XI—Proofs in continuation, extracted from St
quote.text: For that according to John relates His original, effectual, and glorious generation from the Father, thus declaring, “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.”

teachings.title: The Holy Spirit is God
teachings.detail: The Holy Spirit is fully God, not just a force or influence coming from God.
teachings.cap: The Holy Spirit is God: the line joins the Spirit to the one God.
teachings.meaning: The Holy Spirit is not a lesser being, a created messenger, or an impersonal power that God sends out, the way heat comes from a fire. He has the one divine essence fully, just as the Father and the Son do, so He is not a second or third God but the one true God. He is also a Person: He knows, acts, and can be lied to, which could never be said of a mere force. He is equal to the Father and the Son in glory, and He is to be worshipped and trusted in the same way.
teachings.support: In Acts 5:3–4, Peter first says Ananias lied “to the Holy Spirit” and then says he lied “to God,” speaking of the Spirit as God Himself. In 1 Corinthians 3:16, Paul calls believers “God’s temple” because “God’s Spirit dwells in you.” In 1 Corinthians 6:19, he calls the body “a temple of the Holy Spirit.” A temple is the house where God lives, so the Spirit living in us is God Himself living in us. No single verse here spells out the whole teaching, but taken together they show the Bible treating the Spirit as fully God.

verses.label: Acts 5:3–4
verses.text: Then Peter said, “Ananias, how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and withhold some of the proceeds from the land? Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? How could you conceive such a deed in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God!”

verses.label: 1 Corinthians 3:16
verses.text: Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?

verses.label: 1 Corinthians 6:19
verses.text: Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;

topic.title: Is the Holy Spirit fully God, coequal and coeternal with the Father and the Son?
topic.theme: The Holy Spirit's Deity and Personhood
topic.cmp: All the authors (Ambrose, Basil, Gregory of Nyssa, Augustine, Hilary, Novatian, Irenaeus, Athanasius, Owen, Edwards, Bickersteth, Warfield) affirm that the Holy Spirit is fully God, uncreated, coeternal and equal with the Father and the Son, and owed the same faith and worship.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: It is plain then that that, from share in which all creation is excluded, is something special and peculiar to uncreated being.

teachings.title: The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are distinct Persons
teachings.detail: Father, Son and Spirit are three real Persons, each distinct from the others, yet one God.
teachings.cap: Three distinct Persons. Every dashed line reads “is not”.
teachings.meaning: In speaking of God, a “Person” is who someone is, not what someone is. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are three real “Whos,” each able to love, speak and act, and each truly different from the other two. But They are not three separate beings or three Gods, because each Person is the whole of the one God and shares the one divine essence completely. This also rules out the idea that God is one Person who simply takes turns appearing as Father, then Son, then Spirit, like one actor wearing three masks.
teachings.support: In Matthew 3:16–17 all three appear at the same moment: the Son is coming up out of the water, the Spirit descends and rests on Him, and the Father speaks from heaven about “My beloved Son.” In John 14:16–17 Jesus asks the Father, and the Father gives “another Advocate,” the Spirit, so One asks, One gives, and One is sent; They cannot be the same Person. These passages show clearly that the three are distinct, while the truth that They are still one God comes from reading them alongside the many passages that teach there is only one God.

verses.label: Matthew 3:16–17
verses.text: As soon as Jesus was baptized, He went up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens were opened, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him. And a voice from heaven said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased!”

verses.label: John 14:16–17
verses.text: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever— the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.

topic.title: Are the Father, Son and Holy Spirit really distinct Persons in one undivided substance?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that the Father, Son and Holy Spirit are really distinct and not one Person under several names, and they reject Sabellius, Noetus and Praxeas while holding one God.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: How It Was Brought About that the Greeks Speak of Three…
quote.text: there is both Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit; and that the Son is not the same with the Father, nor the Holy Spirit the same with the Father or the Son

teachings.title: The Father is not the Son
teachings.detail: The Father and the Son are two different Persons, not one Person with two names.
teachings.cap: The Father is not the Son.
teachings.meaning: The Father and the Son are truly distinct from each other, and always have been. The Father is the One who begets, and the Son is the One who is begotten; these roles cannot be swapped or blurred together. This rules out the idea that God is a single Person who sometimes acts as the Father and at other times appears as the Son, like one actor changing masks. Yet being distinct does not mean being separate: the Father and the Son are not two Gods, because each has the one divine essence fully.
teachings.support: In John 17:1–5 Jesus lifts His eyes to heaven and prays to the Father, speaking to Him as “You” and asking for “the glory I had with You before the world existed.” No one truly prays to himself or shares glory “with” himself, and glory shared before creation shows that the Son was distinct from the Father before He became man, not only during His life on earth. In John 8:17–18 Jesus appeals to the rule that “the testimony of two men is valid” and counts Himself and the Father as two witnesses, which only works if They are two distinct Persons; that They are nonetheless one God is drawn from other passages read alongside these.

verses.label: John 17:1–5
verses.text: When Jesus had spoken these things, He lifted up His eyes to heaven and said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, that Your Son may glorify You. For You granted Him authority over all people, so that He may give eternal life to all those You have given Him. Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent. I have glorified You on earth by accomplishing the work You gave Me to do. And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.

verses.label: John 8:17–18
verses.text: Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid. I am One who testifies about Myself, and the Father, who sent Me, also testifies about Me.”

topic.title: If the Son has all that the Father has, why is he not the Father?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Augustine, Waterland, and Gregory of Nyssa all deny that the Son's full possession of what the Father is makes Him the Father or strips Him of His own existence.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: The Word of God is in All Things Equal to the Father,…
quote.text: is altogether that which the Father is, yet is not the Father, because the one is Son, the other is Father

teachings.title: The Son is not the Holy Spirit
teachings.detail: The Son and the Holy Spirit are distinct Persons; Jesus calls the Spirit another Helper.
teachings.cap: The Son is not the Holy Spirit.
teachings.meaning: The Son and the Holy Spirit are both fully God, yet They are not one Person going by two names. Nor is the Spirit simply Jesus Himself, present in a new way after He returned to heaven. They are not told apart by being different kinds of God or by one being greater, but only by how each comes from the other Persons. The Son is begotten of the Father, while the Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, as from one source; these are two different ways of coming forth, both without beginning, so the Son and the Spirit share one divine life while each remains truly Himself.
teachings.support: In John 14:16 Jesus promises that the Father will give “another Advocate,” which shows that the Spirit is someone other than Jesus, who had been the disciples’ helper while He was with them. In John 15:26 Jesus says He will send the Spirit, and that the Spirit “will testify about Me”; the one who sends is not the one who is sent, and the one who testifies is not the one He testifies about, so these are two distinct Persons. That verse speaks of the Spirit proceeding from the Father, and the church’s teaching that He proceeds from the Son as well is drawn from reading it together with the rest of Scripture, which calls Him the Spirit of the Son and shows that all the Father has belongs to the Son too.

verses.label: John 14:16
verses.text: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever—

verses.label: John 15:26
verses.text: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father—He will testify about Me.

topic.title: Which Scripture passages show the Persons to be distinct?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Daniel Waterland and Benjamin B.

quote.author: Daniel Waterland
quote.text: it is manifest that the Father and Son are there spoken of, as of two Persons; and one as Anowvng, the other as not knowing, though only in a certain respect

teachings.title: The Holy Spirit is not the Father
teachings.detail: The Holy Spirit is a different Person from the Father, sent by Him and speaking of Him.
teachings.cap: The Holy Spirit is not the Father.
teachings.meaning: The Father and the Holy Spirit are the one God and share the one divine essence, but They are not the same Person. The Spirit is not the Father under another name, or the Father acting in a different way. The Father gives and sends, and the Spirit is given and sent. What tells Them apart is how They are related: the Father comes from no one, while the Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father and the Son, as from one source. This is a difference of relation, not of rank, for the Spirit is fully and equally God with the Father.
teachings.support: In John 14:16–17 Jesus asks the Father, and the Father gives “another Advocate,” the Spirit of truth. The One who gives and the One who is given are clearly two Persons, not one Person seen in two ways. In John 14:26 the Father sends the Spirit “in My name,” which ties the Spirit’s coming to the Son as well. This sending happened in time and is not itself the Spirit’s eternal procession. But the church has drawn from these and other passages that the Spirit is sent in time from the Father and the Son because He eternally proceeds from Them.

verses.label: John 14:16–17, 26
verses.text: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever— the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you. But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.

topic.title: Is the Holy Spirit a distinct Person who acts by his own sovereign will?
topic.theme: The Holy Spirit's Deity and Personhood
topic.cmp: All the authors who answer agree that the Holy Spirit is a personal agent who acts freely, and nearly all rest on the same text, 1 Corinthians 12:11 ("dividing to every man severally as he will"), alongside Acts 13:2 on setting apart Barnabas and Saul.

quote.author: John Owen
quote.place: The Doctrine of the Holy Trinity Explained and Vindicated
quote.text: such things were everywhere ascribed unto him in the Scripture as uncontrollably evidence him to be an intelligent, voluntary agent. This they found so plain and evident, that they could not deny but that he was a person

teachings.title: Each Person is fully God
teachings.detail: Each Person is fully God, not one-third of God.
teachings.cap: Each line carries the whole of God. No Person is a third of God.
teachings.meaning: God is not split into three pieces, with the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit each holding a share. God has no parts, so each Person has the whole of what God is: all His power, wisdom, holiness and life. This is why the Son and the Spirit are not lesser or partial gods, and why they are not three Gods either: there is only one divine essence, and each Person has all of it. We worship one God, and whether we pray to the Father, the Son or the Spirit, we are speaking to the whole God.
teachings.support: In Colossians 2:9, Paul says that “all the fullness of the Deity” dwells in Christ, not a part or a portion of it. Hebrews 1:3 calls the Son “the exact representation of His nature,” which only someone who fully shares that nature could be. In Acts 5:3–4, Peter treats lying “to the Holy Spirit” as having “lied … to God,” and since Scripture takes for granted that the Father is God, these passages taken together, though no single verse says it of all three, lead to the teaching that each Person is wholly God.

verses.label: Colossians 2:9
verses.text: For in Christ all the fullness of the Deity dwells in bodily form.

verses.label: Hebrews 1:3
verses.text: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

verses.label: Acts 5:3–4
verses.text: Then Peter said, “Ananias, how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and withhold some of the proceeds from the land? Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? How could you conceive such a deed in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God!”

topic.title: Does distinguishing the Persons imply composition, inequality or corporeality?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Gregory of Nyssa, Augustine and Irenaeus all deny that distinguishing the Persons brings composition, inequality or corporeality into God, but each argues on different ground.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: For our statement does not hereby violate the simplicity of the Godhead, since community and specific difference are not essence, so that the conjunction of these should render the subject composite

teachings.title: The three Persons are coeternal
teachings.detail: None came into existence after another.
teachings.cap: No Person came first. All three have always been.
teachings.meaning: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit have each existed forever, with no beginning. The Father did not exist alone for a while and then bring the Son and the Spirit into being. This rules out the idea that the Son or the Spirit was created, or is a later and lesser being. When the Bible calls the Son “begotten” of the Father, or says the Spirit comes from the Father, it describes an eternal relationship, not a starting point in time. The Father has always been Father, and so He has always had His Son, and the Spirit has always been with Them both.
teachings.support: In John 1:1–3 the Word, who is the Son, already “was” in the beginning. All things were made through Him, so He cannot be one of the things that were made. In John 17:5 Jesus speaks of the glory He shared with the Father “before the world existed,” and in Hebrews 9:14 the Spirit is called “the eternal Spirit.” No single verse states that all three are coeternal. The teaching is drawn from these passages together, alongside the Bible’s steady witness that God Himself is without beginning.

verses.label: John 1:1–3
verses.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was with God in the beginning. Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made.

verses.label: John 17:5
verses.text: And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.

verses.label: Hebrews 9:14
verses.text: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God!

topic.title: Is the Son eternal, or was there a time when he was not?
topic.theme: The Son's Eternity and Pre-existence
topic.cmp: All the authors (Hilary, Gregory of Nyssa, Athanasius, Augustine, Basil, Novatian, Ambrose, Irenaeus, Waterland, Owen, Bickersteth, Warfield) agree that the Son is eternal and that there was no time when he was not, and most rest this on the correlation of Father and Son (an eternal Father requires an eternal Son), on the Son's being God's Word, Wisdom, Power, Life and Truth, which God was never without, and on the radiance-and-light analogy.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: we have always maintained the birth existing out of time

teachings.title: The three Persons are coequal in deity
teachings.detail: None is inferior in divine nature.
teachings.cap: Every side is equal: none is lesser in divine nature.
teachings.meaning: The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not ranked as greater and lesser Gods. Each Person has the whole of the one divine essence, so each is equally almighty, equally holy, equally glorious and equally worthy of our worship. This rules out any idea that the Son is a lower, created god or that the Spirit is merely a power or force. The Persons are told apart only by how They are related to one another, not by any difference in rank or in how much They are God, and when the Son became man and obeyed the Father, He did not become any less God.
teachings.support: In John 5:23, Jesus says all should honour the Son “just as they honor the Father.” The honour owed to God alone may not be given to anyone less than God, so the Son must be God in the same full way as the Father. Philippians 2:6 says that the Son was “existing in the form of God” and already had “equality with God” before He humbled Himself, while Matthew 28:19 places the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit side by side under one divine name, with no hint that any is lower than the others; taken together with the rest of Scripture, these passages lead to the conclusion that all three Persons are fully equal.

verses.label: John 5:23
verses.text: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.

verses.label: Philippians 2:6
verses.text: Who, existing in the form of God, did not consider equality with God something to be grasped,

verses.label: Matthew 28:19
verses.text: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

topic.title: Is the Son inferior or subordinate to the Father?
topic.theme: The Son's Equality and Texts of Subordination
topic.cmp: All the authors deny that the Son is inferior to the Father in nature, power, glory or honour.

quote.author: Novatian
quote.place: But that God, the Son of God, Born of God the Father…
quote.text: Thus making Himself obedient to His Father in all things, although He also is God, yet He shows the one God the Father by His obedience, from whom also He drew His beginning.

teachings.title: There are exactly three divine Persons
teachings.detail: Not three manifestations of one Person.
teachings.cap: Three real Persons, counted one, two, three. Not one Person appearing in three ways.
teachings.meaning: God is not one Person who takes turns appearing as the Father, then as the Son, then as the Spirit, the way one actor might play three parts or one man might be a father, a son and a worker. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are truly distinct from one another, always and all at the same time, and They really know, love and speak to one another. Yet They are not three Gods, because each Person is the whole one God. There are no more and no fewer than three: the Father who begets, the Son who is begotten, and the Spirit who proceeds.
teachings.support: In Matthew 28:19 Jesus speaks of one “name,” yet lists the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit side by side, each named in turn as distinct from the others. In 2 Corinthians 13:14 Paul likewise names all three together, and each gives something to the church: grace, love and fellowship. Neither verse says in so many words that there are exactly three Persons. That is a conclusion drawn from passages like these together with the wider witness of the Bible, such as the Son praying to the Father and promising to send the Spirit, which shows Them as real Persons relating to one another, not one Person changing roles.

verses.label: Matthew 28:19
verses.text: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

verses.label: 2 Corinthians 13:14
verses.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.

topic.title: Are the Son and Spirit only temporary modes or expansions of one God?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Ambrose and Athanasius agree in rejecting the view that the Son and Spirit are temporary forms or mere names of the one God, but they argue on different grounds.

quote.author: Ambrose of Milan
quote.text: whereas the distinction between the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit always abiding and unchangeable, preserves the Unity of its power.

teachings.title: The Persons mutually indwell one another
teachings.detail: This is called perichoresis.
teachings.cap: Arrows both ways: each Person dwells in the others.
teachings.meaning: Perichoresis is a Greek word for the way the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit live in one another. Each Person is wholly in the other two, not partly, and They share one divine life, so where One is, the Others are too; They have never been apart and never could be. Yet They do not blend into a single Person: the Father is still the Father, the Son is still the Son, and the Spirit is still the Spirit. This also rules out picturing Them as three separate beings who merely work well together, like close friends, because Their unity is far deeper: They are one God.
teachings.support: In John 14:10–11 Jesus says twice that He is in the Father and the Father is in Him. He shows that this is real: the Father dwells in Him and does His works through Him, yet Jesus still speaks of the Father as distinct from Himself. In John 17:21 He prays, “You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You,” again naming two Persons who dwell in each other without becoming one Person, and He asks that believers may also be in Them, which happens by grace and does not make us God. These passages speak of the Father and the Son, so the teaching that the Spirit shares this indwelling is a conclusion drawn from the wider Bible witness that the Spirit is fully God, one with the Father and the Son.

verses.label: John 14:10–11
verses.text: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words I say to you, I do not speak on My own. Instead, it is the Father dwelling in Me, performing His works. Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me—or at least believe on account of the works themselves.

verses.label: John 17:21
verses.text: that all of them may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You. May they also be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.

topic.title: What does the mutual indwelling of the Persons mean?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Hilary of Poitiers and Basil of Caesarea agree that the Father being in the Son and the Son in the Father expresses one shared nature while the Persons stay distinct.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: to confess the Father in the Son and the Son in the Father through the unity of an indivisible nature, not confused but inseparable, not intermingled but identical, not conjoined but coexisting

teachings.title: The Father is eternally Father
teachings.detail: Fatherhood is not a temporary role.
teachings.cap: The Father has always been Father of the Son. It is not a role He took up.
teachings.meaning: God did not become Father at some point, such as when He made the world or when Jesus was born in Bethlehem. He has always been Father, because the Son has always been His Son; there was never a time when the Father was without the Son. Being Father is not a job God took on, a title He wears, or a mask He uses for a season. It is who this Person truly and eternally is, and this rules out the idea that the one God simply plays different roles one after another, or that the Son came into being later.
teachings.support: In John 17:5, Jesus prays to the Father about the glory He shared “with You before the world existed,” so the Father and the Son were already together before anything was created. In John 17:24, Jesus says the Father “loved Me before the foundation of the world,” which shows a real love between Father and Son that is older than creation itself. These verses do not use the words “eternally Father.” But taken together with the Bible’s wider teaching that the Son has always existed, they lead to this conclusion: since the Son has always been the Son, the Father has always been the Father.

verses.label: John 17:5, 24
verses.text: And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed. Father, I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am, that they may see the glory You gave Me because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.

topic.title: Has God always been Father, and is 'Father' a relative name?
topic.theme: God the Father
topic.cmp: Gregory of Nyssa, Hilary of Poitiers and Augustine all treat 'Father' as a relative name that implies the Son, but they develop the point in different directions.

quote.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quote.text: But if the First Father has no cause transcending His own state, and the subsistence of the Son is invariably implied in the title of Father, why do they try to scare us

teachings.title: The Son is eternally begotten of the Father
teachings.detail: Begotten, not created.
teachings.cap: The arrow runs from the Father to the Son: eternally begotten, not created.
teachings.meaning: To say the Son is begotten means He comes from the Father by sharing the Father’s own nature, not by being made. There is a real difference here: what is begotten is the same kind as the one who begets it, while what is created is of a different and lesser kind, as a house is different from the builder who made it. So the Son is not a creature but fully God, just as the Father is, and this begetting has no beginning: there was never a time when the Son did not exist, and nothing bodily is involved, unlike human parents having a child. Because the Father gives the Son the whole of the one divine essence, God is not divided and no second God appears; the Father and the Son are one God.
teachings.support: In John 1:14 and 1:18 Jesus is called the “one and only Son from the Father,” and verse 18 adds that this Son “is Himself God”: He comes from the Father, yet He is God, not something God made. In John 5:26 the Father has “granted the Son to have life in Himself,” so the Son’s life comes from the Father, yet it is life in Himself, just as the Father’s is, not borrowed life like a creature’s. That this begetting is eternal is not stated in any one verse; it is a conclusion drawn from these passages together with others that show the Son was already with God in the beginning, before anything was made.

verses.label: John 1:14, 18
verses.text: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us. We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth. No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known.

verses.label: John 5:26
verses.text: For as the Father has life in Himself, so also He has granted the Son to have life in Himself.

topic.title: Is the Son truly the Father's natural Son, begotten rather than made or created?
topic.theme: The Eternal Generation of the Son
topic.cmp: All the authors agree that the Son is the Father's true, natural Son, begotten from His substance and neither created nor adopted.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: The creation of the world is sufficient evidence to me that Thou art wise; and I am sure that Thy Wisdom, Who is like Thee, must have been begotten from Thyself.

teachings.title: The Holy Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father and the Son
teachings.detail: The Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son together, as from one source.
teachings.cap: The Spirit proceeds eternally from the Father and the Son, as from one source.
teachings.meaning: “Procession” is the word for the way the Holy Spirit eternally comes from God. It differs from the Son’s being begotten. The Son comes from the Father alone, while the Spirit comes from the Father and the Son together, as from one source, not two. The Son has this from the Father, because the Father gives Him everything that is His, including being the source of the Spirit. None of this means the Spirit had a beginning or is less than the Father and the Son: He receives the whole divine nature and is fully God, and His eternal procession is not the same as His being sent at Pentecost.
teachings.support: In John 15:26 Jesus says the Spirit “proceeds from the Father,” yet He also says that He Himself will send the Spirit, and Galatians 4:6 calls Him “the Spirit of His Son.” In John 16:14–15 the Spirit takes from what is the Son’s, and Jesus gives the reason: “Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine.” So what the Spirit receives from the Father, He receives from the Son as well. No single verse says all of this, but taken together these passages lead to the church’s teaching: the Spirit eternally comes forth from the Father and the Son as one source, and the Son has this from the Father.

verses.label: John 15:26
verses.text: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father—He will testify about Me.

verses.label: John 16:14–15
verses.text: He will glorify Me by taking from what is Mine and disclosing it to you. Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine. That is why I said that the Spirit will take from what is Mine and disclose it to you.

verses.label: Galatians 4:6
verses.text: And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!”

topic.title: How does the Holy Spirit proceed, and does He proceed from the Son as well as the Father?
topic.theme: The Spirit's Procession, Names and Mission
topic.cmp: All the authors who address the question affirm that the Spirit proceeds from or belongs to the Son as well as the Father, but they ground and qualify this differently.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: What It is that Suffices Here to Solve the Question Why…
quote.text: if He, too, was called a Son, He would certainly be called the Son of both, which is most absurd, since no one is son of two, save of father and mother

teachings.title: The Persons are distinguished by eternal relations of origin
teachings.detail: Not by different divine natures.
teachings.cap: Only these relations tell the Persons apart. The nature in the centre is one and the same.
teachings.meaning: “Relations of origin” means the ways the three Persons are related to one another by where each comes from, or does not come from. The Father comes from no one; the Son is begotten of the Father; and the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, as from one source. These relations are the only thing that makes the Father, the Son and the Spirit distinct, because in everything else, such as power, glory, wisdom and love, They share the one divine nature completely. So the Persons are not told apart by one being more divine, having a different kind of nature, holding a higher rank or existing first. This “origin” has no beginning in time, and it does not make the Son or the Spirit any less God.
teachings.support: In John 1:18 Jesus is called “the one and only Son,” who is “Himself God” and is “at the Father’s side.” He is fully God, yet distinct from the Father, and what marks Him out is that He is the Son of the Father. In John 15:26 the Spirit “proceeds from the Father” and is sent by the Son, so He too is marked out by where He comes from, not by being a lesser God. That the Spirit proceeds from the Son as well, and that these relations alone distinguish the Persons, is a conclusion drawn from these verses together with the rest of Scripture, which also calls Him the Spirit of the Son.

verses.label: John 1:18
verses.text: No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father’s side, has made Him known.

verses.label: John 15:26
verses.text: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father—the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father—He will testify about Me.

topic.title: Which things are said of God substantially, and which relatively?
topic.theme: Persons, Essence and Their Distinction
topic.cmp: Augustine's distinction between absolute and relative predication, the reply to the Arian claim that every predicate names God's substance, and whether anything is said of God by accident.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: He proceeds to refute those arguments which the heretics…
quote.text: some things are also predicated of Him relatively, i.e. not in respect to Himself, but to something not Himself, as He is called Father in respect to the Son, and Lord in respect to the creature that serveth Him

teachings.title: The Father loves the Son eternally
teachings.detail: The love between the Father and the Son did not begin at creation; it has always been.
teachings.cap: The Father has loved the Son from before the world began.
teachings.meaning: Before God made anything, the Father and the Son were already sharing a perfect love, so God did not need to create the world, or us, in order to have someone to love. This rules out the idea that God was lonely before creation, or that His love for the Son began when Jesus was born, baptised or raised from the dead. Because God does not change, this love has never grown, faded or started; it belongs to who God eternally is. It also shows why love is not just something God does now and then but lies at the heart of His very being, and the love He shows us flows out of this love He has always had within Himself.
teachings.support: In John 17:24, Jesus, praying to His Father, says the Father loved Him “before the foundation of the world,” that is, before anything was created. The verse itself places this love before creation. To say it had no beginning at all is a conclusion drawn when this verse is read together with the Bible’s wider teaching that the Son has always existed with the Father and that God never changes.

verses.label: John 17:24
verses.text: Father, I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am, that they may see the glory You gave Me because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.

topic.title: Is the Holy Spirit properly named Love and Gift within the Trinity?
topic.theme: The Spirit's Procession, Names and Mission
topic.cmp: Augustine of Hippo is the chief advocate of naming the Holy Spirit Love and Gift: he argues that the Spirit is the consubstantial communion and mutual love of Father and Son, is specially called by what both share in common ('Spirit', 'holy', love), and is relational as Gift, so that he is not a Son because he comes forth as given rather than born.

quote.author: Augustine of Hippo
quote.place: The Holy Spirit Also is Equal to the Father and the Son…
quote.text: Therefore the Holy Spirit, whatever it is, is something common both to the Father and Son. But that communion itself is consubstantial and co-eternal

teachings.title: The Son eternally shares the Father’s glory
teachings.detail: Before the world began, the Son shared the Father’s glory as one equal with Him.
teachings.cap: The glory runs both ways: the Son shared it with the Father before the world existed.
teachings.meaning: In the Bible, God’s glory is the shining fullness of who He is: His greatness, beauty and majesty. The Son did not receive this glory at some point, earn it, or borrow it. He has always shared it with the Father, because He has the same divine nature. This rules out any idea that the Son is a created being or a lesser God, since God gives His own glory to no creature. When the Son became man in the Incarnation, His glory was hidden behind His humble human life, but it was never lost.
teachings.support: In John 17:5, Jesus speaks of “the glory I had with You before the world existed,” so He existed before creation and already shared the Father’s glory then. He does not ask for something new, but for that same glory to be shown in His life as a man. That this sharing has no beginning and is a sharing as equals is a conclusion drawn from this verse together with the wider teaching of Scripture that only God has divine glory and that the Son is God.

verses.label: John 17:5
verses.text: And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.

topic.title: What does it mean to glorify God, and how is the Son glorified with the Father?
topic.theme: Worship, Glory and Baptism in the Triune Name
topic.cmp: The authors agree that glorifying God adds nothing to him and that the Son shares the Father's glory rather than lacking it, but they come at the topic from different angles.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: He had not lost His former being, but He had become what He was not before; He had not abdicated His own position, yet He had taken ours; He prays that the nature which He had assumed may be promoted to the glory which He had never renounced.

teachings.title: The three Persons have one divine will
teachings.detail: Not three competing divine wills.
teachings.cap: All three share the one will at the centre, not three wills side by side.

note.title: One divine will, and Jesus’ human will
note.text: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit share one divine will. In becoming human, the Son also assumed a human will. Jesus’ prayer in Gethsemane expresses His human obedience to the Father, not disagreement within God’s divine will.

teachings.meaning: A will is the power to choose and to want. It belongs to what God is, His one essence, not to each Person on His own. So the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are not like three people who each have their own wishes and must agree on a plan; They share one divine will, though each Person wills in His own way, in keeping with how He is related to the Others. This rules out any idea of the Persons disagreeing, bargaining or overruling one another. It does not deny that the Son, when He became man, also took a real human will, which always freely followed the one divine will.
teachings.support: In John 5:19 Jesus says the Son can do nothing by Himself and does whatever the Father does, which shows that the Father and the Son never act from separate purposes but in one shared work. In John 10:30 Jesus says that He and the Father are one, pointing to a oneness deeper than simple agreement. Neither verse uses the words “one will”; the teaching is a conclusion drawn from these and other passages together, which show one God acting with one purpose, and from the truth that the Persons share one divine essence.

verses.label: John 5:19
verses.text: So Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father does, the Son also does.

verses.label: John 10:30
verses.text: I and the Father are one.”

topic.title: Do Christ's sayings of dependence mean the Son lacks his own divine power and will?
topic.theme: The Son's Equality and Texts of Subordination
topic.cmp: Hilary, Basil and Bickersteth agree that Christ's sayings of dependence do not mean the Son lacks his own divine power or will.

quote.author: Hilary of Poitiers
quote.text: Through the birth the nature of God is abiding in the Son, and does that which He Himself does. What He does God does, but what God does in Him, He Himself does

teachings.title: The three Persons act inseparably in divine works
teachings.detail: Particular works are still attributed to particular Persons.
teachings.cap: Every work is from the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit, and it is one act of the one God.
teachings.meaning: When God acts in the world, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit do not split the work into three separate jobs. They do one work together, because They are one God with one will and one power. Yet the Bible often links a particular work with one Person: creation with the Father, redemption with the Son, and making us holy with the Spirit. This is called appropriation, and it shows what is especially fitting to each Person without implying that the other two are absent or idle, so it rules out picturing the Trinity as a team that hands out separate tasks.
teachings.support: In John 5:19 Jesus says the Son “can do nothing by Himself” and that “whatever the Father does, the Son also does.” This is not because the Son is lesser, but because the Father and the Son never work apart; They share one work. In 1 Corinthians 12:4–6 Paul links gifts with the Spirit, ministries with the Lord Jesus, and ways of working with God the Father, yet insists that “the same God works all things in all people,” so each work is linked to one Person while none works alone; the full teaching is drawn from passages like these taken together rather than stated in one verse.

verses.label: John 5:19
verses.text: So Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father does, the Son also does.

verses.label: 1 Corinthians 12:4–6
